'''Laszlo Bela Kish''' (born László Béla Kiss) is a physicist and professor of [[Electrical Engineering|Electrical and Computer Engineering]] at [[Texas A&M University]].  His activities<ref name=publist>[http://www.ece.tamu.edu/~noise/publist.pdf Publication list of Laszlo Kish]</ref> include a wide range of issues surrounding the physics and technical applications of stochastic fluctuations (noises) in physical, biological and technological systems, including [[nanotechnology]]. His earlier ''long-term positions'' include the [[University of Szeged|Department of Experimental Physics, University of Szeged, Hungary (JATE, 1982–1997)]], and [[Uppsala University|Angstrom Laboratory, Uppsala University, Sweden (1997–2001)]]. During the same periods he had also conducted scientific research in short-term  positions, such as at the [[Eindhoven University of Technology]] (Netherlands, 1986, 1997),<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.tue.nl/en/university/column-1/about-the-university/ |title=About the University |access-date=2011-05-29 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110607025043/http://www.tue.nl/en/university/column-1/about-the-university |archive-date=2011-06-07 }}</ref> [[University of Cologne]] (Germany, 1989, 1990), National Research Laboratory of Metrology (Japan, 1991),<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.aist.go.jp/NRLM/english/ |title=Archived copy |access-date=2011-05-29 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110722004212/http://www.aist.go.jp/NRLM/english/ |archive-date=2011-07-22 }}</ref> [[University of Birmingham]] (United Kingdom, 1993), and others.

==Education==
He received his MS in physics from [[JATE|Attila József University (JATE)]], [[Hungary]], 1980; and doctoral degree in [[solid state physics]], at JATE in 1984. He had no official PhD adviser, though his mentors were Laszlo Vize and Miklos Torok. He received a [[docent]] in [[solid state physics]] ([[habilitation]]) from [[Uppsala University]], [[Sweden]], in 1994. He received a Doctor of Science (physics), from the [[Hungarian Academy of Sciences]] in 2001.

==Research==
{{confusing|date=March 2012}}
His main areas of interest<ref name=publist/> have been related to stochastic fluctuations (noise), especially those related to the relevant laws, limits and applications, including the addressing of new or open questions, or exposing fashionable misconceptions. He has/had been working in many related fields, (see his list of publications<ref name=publist/>) such as 1/f noise and its models, stochastic resonance, high-Tc superconductors, noise at percolation and biased percolation,  nanoparticles and their lognormal size distribution, self-organized criticality, universal conductance fluctuations, the error–speed–power dissipation issues of physical informatics, noise as information and information carrier, chemical and biological sensing, secure communication, unconventional computation, vibration-induced fluctuation analysis of soils, electronic device noise vs its degradation, weight fluctuations of memory devices during/after writing/deletion of information, etc. He has often played the role of a critic.<ref name=mythbuster>[http://www.ece.tamu.edu/~noise/research_files/mythbuster.html Myth-busting in Physics and Information Technology, webpage at Texas A&M University]</ref> His inventions and co-inventions include<ref name=publist/> ''[[fluctuation-enhanced sensing]]'', [[sensing of phage-triggered ion cascades (SEPTIC)|''SEPTIC method'' (prompt bacterium detection)]], secure communication with Johnson-like noise (''[http://sites.google.com/site/kishcypher/ Kish cypher]''), ''speed–error–energy limits of computers'',<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.ece.tamu.edu/%7Enoise/research_files/research_dissip.htm|title = Electrical and Computer Engineering}}</ref> ''zero-signal-power communication'', "[[Information-theoretic security|information theoretically secure]] computer hardware",<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.ece.tamu.edu/%7Enoise/research_files/secure_hardware.htm|title = Electrical and Computer Engineering}}</ref> ''[[noise-based logic]]'', [http://www.ece.tamu.edu/%7Enoise/research_files/noise_engines.htm ''Electrical noise engines''] and others.

==Public activity==

He was the founding editor-in-chief of ''[[Fluctuation and Noise Letters]]'' (2001–2008), where he is currently Honorary Editor (2009–present). Kish is the founder of the international conference series [http://upon4.unile.it/history.html ''Unsolved Problems of Noise''] (held at various locations at every 3rd years since 1996 when he chaired the first meeting). He is co-founder of SPIE's international conference series [http://www.quiprocone.org/FN04_CALL_v.pdf ''Fluctuations and Noise''] (with [[Derek Abbott|D. Abbott]]) and the [http://www.ece.tamu.edu/%7Enoise/HotPI_2013/HotPI_2013.html ''Hot Topics of Physical Informatics'' (HotPI)] conference series (with [[David K. Ferry]] and He Wen). He coauthored the HTML document available for download from the internet,  ''The Dancer and the Piper: Resolving Problems with Government Research Contracting''.

==Honors==

He was the recipient of the year 2001 Benzelius Prize of the Royal Society of Science of Sweden for his activities on ''[[fluctuation-enhanced sensing|fluctuation-enhanced chemical sensing]]''. In 2011, he received the title of [https://web.archive.org/web/20110318090728/http://www.ece.tamu.edu/NewsAndEvents/Newsletter/Vol11No2/news_kishhonor.php Honorary  Doctor (''Honoris Causa'')] from [[List of Uppsala University People|Uppsala University]], Sweden for his achievement in "research and technical applications of random fluctuations and [[Noise (electronics)|noise]]."  In 2012, he received the title of {{Deprecated archive|url=https://archive.today/20130217101406/http://www.ece.tamu.edu/NewsAndEvents/Newsletter/Vol12No6/news_kish.php|title=Honorary Doctor (''Honoris Causa'')}} from the [[University of Szeged#Notable alumni and professors|University of Szeged]] for his "outstanding research work and achievements."
